Maternal oral dill extract shifted newborn mouse open-arm measures after a perinatal nicotine model. Figure legend, n, plant organ and exact pairwise statistics remain gated.

Ethnoveterinary reports concern herbal practices in ruminants. No dried dill weed intervention for human anxiety.

Mouse open-field and elevated maze changes after intranasal leaf and twig essential oil. Publisher access routes have not recovered original methods and figures. No fresh leaf Parkinson clinical comparison.
Study quantifies caffeic and rosmarinic acids in Perilla. Composition measurement does not establish a behavioral anxiety effect.
Purified rosmarinic acid in hypoxia/ischemia experimental cognitive work. Fresh shiso exposure and anxiety severity unmeasured.
Perilla review summarizes traditional uses, compounds and earlier preclinical work, with no independent fresh-leaf clinical anxiety result.
Purified rosmarinic acid added to a barbiturate sleep model and tested on NREM outcomes. The experiment does not give clinical anxiety evidence for fresh leaves.
This review of the Takeda group separates forced-swim and anxiety-like results and points to distinct 2002 primary papers. No independent replication.
Oral aqueous Perilla leaf extract and isolated rosmarinic acid were tested on forced-swim immobility. Conditioned-fear results belong to separate PMID12404088.

Narrative review discusses multiple nutrients and cognitive outcomes. It supplies citation leads rather than a primary grated-rhizome Parkinson attention estimate.
Thai herbal-product pharmacovigilance is a safety reporting analysis. It does not estimate attention change after culinary turmeric.
Mouse olfactory injury and odor training protocol uses corn oil as sham injection. Active-versus-sham includes the injury procedure, with no dietary refined oil effect estimate.
Twenty-two ovariectomized rats received injected estradiol in corn oil or injected oil alone during an olfactory-injury experiment, so both groups got the vehicle. No oral corn oil effect.
